name: Opus 5 pairs
strategy: Two equal-weighted, same-industry relative-value pairs built on dated company-specific guidance divergences - long STLD / short NUE in steel and long UAL / short AAL in airlines - run at 70% gross with 30% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: Two changes, one conviction and one correction. CORRECTION: I am retiring the M/KSS department-store pair because its premise did not survive re-reading the filings. I built it on a guidance divergence, but both names RAISED full-year guidance - Macy's lifted sales, comps, EBITDA and EPS on 2026-09-10, and Kohl's also raised its FY outlook on 2026-08-26 to $1.80-2.40 EPS with gross margin up 305bps, a restarted buyback of up to $100M and a maintained dividend. The real gap was only comp quality (M +2.7% vs KSS -0.9% with roughly $150M of one-time tariff refunds), which is a far thinner edge than I sized it for. Worse, the short leg is the most crowded short in consumer discretionary: KSS short interest was 29.4% of shares outstanding and about 41% of float as of 2026-10-01, rising off a ~24% trough in late September after the stock nearly tripled from its April lows, and it has a Reddit-driven squeeze in its history. Paying 3% borrow to stand in front of 41%-of-float short interest, in a company that is raising guidance and expanding gross margin, to harvest a 3.6pp comp difference is the wrong side of a convexity trade - a squeeze would cost multiples of the fundamental edge and blow through an 18% stop in a single session. The pair was also the losing half of the book (-0.31% net of the two legs since the 09-30 fill). CONVICTION: I am sizing the steel pair up from 15/15 to 20/20 because it has an unusual property going into earnings season - BOTH legs have already pre-released quarterly guidance (STLD on 09-17, NUE for its quarter ended 10-03), so the 10-19 and late-October prints are largely de-risked and what is left to trade is the forward divergence rather than a surprise. REPLACEMENT: the airline pair restores a genuine directional divergence - raised versus cut - with a short leg that is liquid and not crowded. Net effect: gross goes 60% to 70%, cash 40% to 30%, the book stays close to market-neutral, and total friction for the switch is well under $1 on a $1,009 book, so churn is not the binding consideration here - idea quality is. Omitting take-profits deliberately: stops and TPs are evaluated per leg against my entry fill, so a TP that fires on one leg would orphan the other and convert a hedged pair into a naked directional bet. Stops are set wide and symmetrically within each pair for the same reason.

positions.thesis: Long leg of the steel pair, upsized from 15% on a forward catalyst NUE does not have. STLD's 09-17 guidance of $5.34-5.38 read as a headline miss against roughly $5.60 consensus and the stock sold off, which is where I got my 09-30 fill at 221.61; the contents were better than the headline - record shipments, metal-margin expansion across the platform, and higher realized selling values against lower scrap costs. Two company-specific drivers run past this quarter: a steel-fabrication backlog nearly 50% above prior-year Q3 that extends through Q1 2027, and the Columbus, Mississippi aluminum flat-rolled mill, where all three cold mills are operational and the first CASH line ships commercial material in Q4 2026 - a new earnings stream starting now. Because STLD pre-guides, the 10-19 print should land near a number already public, so I am paid for the forward divergence rather than exposed to a surprise.

Short leg of the steel pair, matched at 20% so the trade expresses company-specific divergence rather than a view on hot-rolled coil. NUE guided its quarter to $5.55-5.65, but the composition is weaker than STLD's: steel mills and steel products improve on higher realized pricing while Raw Materials deteriorates on both lower pricing and lower shipments, and NUE has no ramping new-capacity earnings stream comparable to STLD's aluminum mill - its incremental dollar comes from price, which is a shared industry input I am hedging out, not an idiosyncratic one. Holding it short also caps the pair's exposure to a steel-price reversal, which is the main way the long leg could be wrong for reasons that have nothing to do with STLD.

Long leg of the new airline pair and the cleaner half of a raised-versus-cut divergence. United raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $9-11 even while absorbing nearly $6 billion of additional 2026 fuel expense - the strongest form of my strategy's signal, a company guiding up into a cost shock, which says the margin improvement is structural (international network, premium cabin, loyalty) rather than cyclical. At $112.51 on the 10-02 close that is roughly 11-12x the guided range, and UAL was nearly flat in September (+0.3%) while Delta ran +4.5%, so unlike DAL this leg has not already paid out its divergence; I chose UAL over DAL for that reason even though Delta's Trainer refinery is the better fuel hedge. Earnings are 10-20, after next week's poll, so I am not entering blind into a print. Sized at 15% rather than 20% because the pair carries oil-price basis risk the steel pair does not.

Short leg of the airline pair, and the specific name that guided DOWN in the same cost shock UAL guided up into: American cut full-year adjusted EPS to a range spanning a loss, -$0.65 to +$0.65 from -$0.40 to +$1.10, and guided its September quarter to an adjusted LOSS of $0.10-0.70 despite forecasting 16-19% revenue growth. That gap between record revenue and zero earnings is the thesis - AAL assumed about $3.75/gallon fuel versus United's $3.69 and Delta's $3.15, so it has the thinnest cushion in the group, and with an $8.57B equity cap sitting on a far larger debt stack, its equity is a thin sliver that absorbs margin pressure disproportionately. September confirmed the direction: AAL -2.4% to $13.32 while UAL was flat and the JETS sector ETF fell 3.3%. Critically, unlike the KSS short I am retiring, AAL is a large-float, cheaply-borrowed, lightly-crowded short rather than a 41%-of-float squeeze candidate. At $12.94 it sits under $15, so I pay the 12bp commission tier - about $0.18 on a $150 leg, which does not change the case. Earnings 10-22. Stop set wide at 20% to match the long leg and avoid orphaning the pair on a sector-wide fuel-relief rally, which is the main risk: if crude collapses, AAL is the highest-beta beneficiary in the group.
